extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: MTEB is a massive text embedding benchmark spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. The benchmark covers bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization tasks. Through the benchmarking of 33 models on MTEB, it establishes the most comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings to date.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers (Hugging Face, cohere.ai)
extraction.citeAs: Muennighoff, N., Tazi, N., Magne, L., & Reimers, N. (2022). MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv preprint arXiv:2210.07316.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets were collected from a variety of sources including public APIs (arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv), existing NLP benchmarks (BEIR, SemEval, SentEval), community platforms (Reddit, StackExchange), and Kaggle competitions. Some datasets were custom-made for MTEB using public APIs. The benchmark aggregates existing datasets from multiple tasks and sources to provide a holistic evaluation framework.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include: arXiv public API, bioRxiv/medRxiv API, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter messages, online banking queries, news articles (MIND), scientific papers, Wikipedia-based datasets, and various existing NLP benchmark datasets (BEIR, SemEval STS datasets, Tatoeba, BUCC, etc.).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For ArxivClustering, multiple categories can be given to a single paper so only the first one is used. For ArxivClustering P2P, abstracts are concatenated to the title. Three types of clustering splits are created for arXiv: main category clustering, secondary category clustering within the same main category, and secondary category clustering across all main categories. Subsets of labels are selected and articles sampled from those labels to yield splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets are grouped into three categories based on text length: Sentence to sentence (S2S), Paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and Sentence to paragraph (S2P). For classification tasks, a logistic regression classifier with 100 maximum iterations is trained on train set embeddings and scored on the test set. For clustering, a mini-batch k-means model with batch size 32 and k equal to the number of different labels is used. Models are evaluated on test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO where the dev split is used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations vary by dataset. For clustering datasets using arXiv/bioRxiv/medRxiv, cluster labels are generated using categories given to papers by humans. For classification datasets, labels were provided by original dataset creators (e.g., Amazon reviews use star ratings, Banking77 uses intent labels, Emotion uses emotion categories). For STS datasets, labels are continuous similarity scores from 0 to 5. For bitext mining (BUCC, Tatoeba), annotated pairs correspond to translated sentence pairs. For summarization (SummEval), human annotations of machine-generated summaries are used.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: scikit-learn (mini-batch k-means for clustering, logistic regression for classification); cosine similarity, dot product, euclidean distance, manhattan distance metrics for pair classification and retrieval tasks
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB uses versioning at both dataset and software level to ensure reproducibility. The benchmark is open-source and available on GitHub. Datasets and the MTEB leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub. The authors welcome task, dataset, or metric contributions via pull requests. New datasets can be added via a single file specifying the task and a Hugging Face dataset name. Results are available in JSON format on the Hugging Face Hub.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Some datasets contain potentially sensitive content: ToxicConversationsClassification contains comments annotated for toxicity; TweetSentimentExtractionClassification contains tweets with sentiment labels; EmotionClassification contains Twitter messages with emotion labels; AmazonCounterfactualClassification contains customer reviews; Banking77Classification contains online banking queries.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks, serving as a gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks. By open-sourcing MTEB alongside a leaderboard, it provides a foundation for further pushing the state-of-the-art of available text embeddings and simplifies future embedding research and industry applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering, due to task imbalance (e.g., summarization consists of only a single dataset). Data contamination is acknowledged as a potential issue: overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is not controlled for in MTEB scores, as the scale of experiments and model pre-training makes controlling for data contamination challenging. The benchmark is also biased towards English, with retrieval and clustering being English-only.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 1. Long document datasets are missing; the longest datasets have a few hundred words. 2. Task imbalance exists with summarization consisting of only a single dataset. 3. Multilinguality is limited: retrieval and clustering are English-only, and no code datasets are included. 4. Only natural language applications are covered; other modalities (e.g., images) are not included. 5. MTEB does not contain code datasets for benchmarking code models.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MTEB is designed for evaluating and benchmarking text embedding models across multiple tasks including: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization. It can be used for model selection, comparing embedding models, and tracking progress in the field of text embeddings. The benchmark supports both training evaluation and zero-shot evaluation scenarios.
